items.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020
items.q: I grew up with all these, Count Basie records. And especially I wrote about that.

ctx.x: So that’s why in my book I wanted to really, trying to find answers about — what I miss also with that, I grew up with all these, Count Basie records. And especially I wrote about that. When you listen to any bassist playing with the orchestra, in Basie’s band the bass line is not the bass line. It’s like a counterpoint voice, which still has the function of a bass line. The bass is singing. And as a caricature today we put the bass just as a groove. So you spend the whole tune just playing [scats], which is…

That’s true. Well, Pierre, we are unfortunately coming to the end of our program. I could have gone asking so many more questions. I have one last question. Last but not least. If you were to take a jazz record on a desert island, what record would it be?
